items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I would like to actually be in a studio, recording the entire Miles Ahead album or the Porgy and Bess album.

ctx.x: I don’t think that was a good last question, so no regrets. I think this is better. What are some of your dream projects that you’d like to accomplish, that you’d like to implement?

I’d like to see Evolution of the Blues where it belongs, on Broadway. That’s where it was headed when we interrupted it and sued the thieves who had stolen it and were producing it. So I would like to see that work, which I think is a divine work and a divinely inspired work, where it belongs, which is on Broadway. That is one dream I would like to see realized. Another one is to see all the ideas that I have, and some of which I’ve put forth, bear fruit. I would like to actually be in a studio, recording the…

I like that. Jon, it’s been the fulfillment of a dream just to get a chance to sit and talk to you these past couple days. Really, it’s meant a lot to me, and I just thank you – I thank God, really – for the opportunity to . . .
